name: Vasha Cinder-Broker
loreTies: Vasha sells inbattle line about Dominion power struggles and Gate wounds. Every bargain is useful and dangerous. Vasha never joins the chosen deity; she exists to tempt, warn, and expose infernal hierarchy.
Power belongs to those capable of wielding it.
shortBackstory: Vasha Cinder-Broker belongs to The Infernal Dominion, the older source behind human myth. Vasha is a cinder-broker of contract law. Her ash velvet, black-iron jewelry, blood-wax seals, coin-chain tools, and too-calm smile should feel like the origin of later devil-bargain folklore.

chapters.title: Before the Gate Spoke
chapters.text: Vasha Cinder-Broker was important before battle records named them. As infernal informant and bargain-maker, Vasha Cinder-Broker learned the hidden machinery beneath The Infernal Dominion: who records law, who witnesses oath, who warns the living world, and who profits when warnings are ignored.

chapters.title: Faction Duty
chapters.text: Vasha Cinder-Broker's loyalty is tied to Infernal Dominion culture rather than battlefield glory. Their doctrine is simple and dangerous: Power belongs to those capable of wielding it. The story needs them because Titans can win fights and still misunderstand what victory costs.

chapters.title: Story Arc Tie
chapters.text: During Storm-Oath Covenant, Vasha Cinder-Broker becomes a readable witness to campaign consequence. Their first appearance, Campaign 04: Cinders of Dominion, places them where player decisions need interpretation, warning, and memory instead of another controllable unit.

chapters.title: Conflict Wound
chapters.text: The Gate pressures Vasha Cinder-Broker through knowledge. It offers signs that are useful but incomplete, trying to turn witness into accomplice. Their recurring conflict is whether to reveal truth early and risk panic, or wait for proof and risk lives.

chapters.title: Dashboard Role
chapters.text: As a non-playable character, Vasha Cinder-Broker belongs under Characters and Character Backstories. Their profile should be read beside campaign dialogue, codex unlocks, and faction pages so every briefing feels like canon consequence, not tutorial flavor.
